data.name: Jegan
data.gender_notes: Jegan is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jegan is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Jagat' meaning world or universe, and 'Anugraha' meaning grace or boon. The name Jegan signifies a divine gift bestowed upon the child, symbolizing the blessings and protection of the gods. The name Jegan carries the meaning “God's Gracious Gift” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jegan usually hope their child will grow to embody god's gracious gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name imbued with the divine grace and blessings of the gods.
data.etymology: Jegan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's Gracious Gift.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jegan total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: Jegan was a renowned Chola warrior from the 9th century CE who served under Rajaraja Chola I. He played a significant role in the expansion of the Chola Empire during this period.

Jegan was also the name of a 13th century CE Tamil poet who wrote in the Sangam literature tradition. His works, which include poems on love, war, and nature, are considered among the greatest contributions to the Tamil literary canon.
